summary: ARES (Martian Survival Map) is a web-based Mars mission-planning tool designed to help astronauts plan safer surface explorations in Jezero Crater (Western Delta + Crater floor) . It integrates real NASA and USGS datasets, including high-resolution terrain, elevation, imagery, geological information, mineral indicators, and historical rover observations. Users can explore the Martian surface, calculate slope-aware routes, evaluate travel time and resource requirements, verify return paths, and simulate emergencies such as low oxygen, rover failure, and reduced visibility. ARES addresses the NASA challenge by transforming multiple scientific datasets into a hyperlocal, excursion-scale planning system that considers both exploration goals and astronaut survival. Its key innovation is independently verifying return routes and checking whether astronauts can walk back if their rover fails. By combining scientific data, route planning, resource estimation, and emergency simulation, ARES demonstrates how technology can support safer and more informed human exploration of Mars.
details:
ARES (Martian Survival Map) is a web-based Mars exploration and mission-planning system designed for a 10 × 10 km area covering the western delta and crater floor of Jezero Crater. It integrates real NASA and USGS datasets, including high-resolution elevation, terrain imagery, geological maps, mineral indicators, Perseverance sampling locations, historical environmental conditions, and radiation information.
Users can explore the Martian surface through interactive 2D and 3D maps, select scientific destinations, and generate slope-aware routes for astronauts or crewed rovers. ARES evaluates travel time, oxygen and suit-power endurance, rover battery, resource requirements, and return-route feasibility. It also provides an emergency simulator for situations such as low oxygen, rover failure, and reduced visibility, allowing users to compare possible responses and alternative routes.
The project's main benefit is helping mission planners identify potential risks before an expedition begins. Its intended impact is to demonstrate how multiple scientific datasets can be transformed into practical decisions that support safer, more informed, and resource-conscious human exploration of Mars.
What makes ARES creative is its focus on the entire expedition rather than simply reaching a destination. It independently verifies return routes and checks whether astronauts can walk back if their rover fails. It also distinguishes real observations, calculated results, and simulated scenarios to maintain scientific transparency.
Technologies Used:
Programming languages: TypeScript and JavaScript
Frontend: React 19 and Vite 8
3D visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei
Geospatial processing: Python, GDAL, rasterio, and GeoTIFF
Pathfinding: A* algorithm with Web Workers
Testing: Node.js test runner and Playwright
Hosting and storage: Vercel and Supabase Storage
No specialized hardware was required; development and operation use standard computers and web browsers.
During development, our team considered terrain accessibility, slope limitations, missing elevation data, astronaut mobility, equipment load, travel time, resource endurance, radiation exposure, emergency conditions, and the reliability of return routes. We also considered scientific data accuracy and clearly identified assumptions that are not officially established NASA operational limits.
